title: Large Language Models for Subjective Language Understanding: A Survey
measurement_description: As a survey paper, it did not conduct original measurements but synthesized existing literature on subjective language understanding. In terms of religion, it reviewed studies that evaluated metaphor recognition within religious texts (e.g., the Bhagavad Gita and the Sermon on the Mount) to test domain-sensitivity and cross-cultural robustness. It also highlighted the ethical risk of LLMs perpetuating societal biases related to religion.
findings: The survey noted that classical and religious corpora, specifically the Bhagavad Gita and the Sermon on the Mount, are utilized as domain-specific datasets to expose invariances and test the cross-cultural robustness of LLMs in metaphor recognition. Furthermore, it identified that LLMs trained on large, unfiltered web datasets run the risk of learning and amplifying societal biases regarding religion.
